open_question_syringe_stroke.finding: head_l's SYR envelope says a 2:1 lever turns the 35 mm pusher stroke into 70 mm at the plunger, but the modelled lever has its input (pusher rod) and output (plunger link) on the same axis, so it gives no ratio; a real 2:1 lever with a 35 mm input and the 28 mm arm the tool has room for would swing about 50 degrees: as drawn, it does not work
open_question_syringe_stroke.redesign: drive a 10 mL luer-lock syringe DIRECTLY from the pusher: about 14.5 mm bore (ASSUMED), so the same 5 mL per fill needs about 30 mm of plunger travel, inside the 35 mm pusher stroke; no lever, no custom mechanism; force at the plunger = pusher thrust (NEMA14: about 185 N, about 0.9 MPa on 165 mm2, far above a jetting need of the order of 0.1-0.2 MPa, ASSUMED); resolution about 0.17 uL per full step at 1 mm lead and 200 steps per rev (CALCULATED)
open_question_syringe_stroke.fallback: a rack-and-pinion stroke doubler (pinion on a pusher-driven slider between a fixed and a moving rack): 2:1, bought racks and pinion, half the force at the plunger; only if the rig shows the 10 mL syringe cannot jet the small volumes
open_question_syringe_stroke.firmware: SYR can be re-armed with stroke <= 35 mm of pusher = plunger; contact window as the other tools; to be proved on the rig

open_question_noz_dy_dock_yf.finding: printer.cfg holds noz_dy -73.5 and dock_yf 545.5.  The coupling axis (= nozzle row centre) is 102.5 mm in front of the beam front face (head_l AXY), so noz_dy = -102.5; with -73.5 every place guard and tip-gate position is 29 mm off in Y.  The two provisional numbers are consistent with each other (545.5 - 73.5 = 472, the rev L dock row), so the dock was aimed right by the firmware's own arithmetic but the real nozzle would come down 29 mm in front of the bay; the real printer Y over the bay row is dock_y + 102.5: L 574.5 (as rev L), M 464.5, S 354.5
